quarterly_data.signal: Third consecutive quarter of record revenue: Q2 sales of $451 million, up 32% sequentially and 127% year over year, well above the guided $393-411 million range. Non-GAAP gross margin was 50.2% (guided 48.5-49.5%), operating margin 23.1% (guided 21-22%) and earnings per ADS $2.43. Operating expenses rose to $122.1 million on new controller/solution development, tape-out costs and headcount. Growth was broad-based with standout contribution from Ferri for automotive, enterprise Boot Drives and embedded eMMC & UFS.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $451M (+32% QoQ, +127% YoY); GM 50.2%; operating margin 23.1%; EPS/ADS $2.43

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue of $519-541 million, up 15-20% sequentially, led by Ferri for Automotive, Enterprise Boot Drive solutions and the new MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. Gross margin guided up to 50-51% on richer mix from MonTitan and PCIe 5 controllers, operating margin stepping up sharply to 27.5-28.5%, tax rate 22%. Full-year 2026 revenue is expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE to a record, with operating margin exceeding 30% exiting the year. Long-term gross-margin target remains 48-50%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $519M-$541M (+15-20% QoQ); GM 50-51%; operating margin 27.5-28.5%; FY2026 revenue >100% growth

quarterly_data.signal: NAND/DRAM scarcity is the defining constraint. CEO Wallace Kou: the AI super cycle has driven substantial HBM, DRAM, NAND and HDD price increases and 'mounting substrate and supply pressure,' and he expects the scarcity to persist 'likely until 2028 when new fabs come online.' DRAM and NAND now account for almost 56% of total BOM cost on a low-end smartphone, forcing OEMs to trim specifications; smartphone units are still expected down 10-15% in 2026. NAND makers are redirecting focus and CapEx to DRAM and HBM, deemphasising eMMC/UFS and exiting automotive - which hands share to Silicon Motion's module-maker customers and gives it stronger pricing power. Long-standing relationships let Silicon Motion secure NAND from multiple suppliers through the shortage, which management calls a significant and enduring differentiator.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND scarcity expected to persist until 2028; DRAM+NAND ~56% of low-end smartphone BOM; smartphone units -10% to -15% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers entered commercial production in Q2 with TWO Tier 1 customers, with five additional Tier 1 customers expected to ramp in the second half. Management reaffirmed the target of 5-10% of total revenue coming from MonTitan exiting 2026. First customers are targeting the compute market with TLC NAND for AI platforms that use NAND for high-speed, low-latency storage dedicated to NEAR-GPU AND NEAR-CPU KV CACHE. TLC-based solutions are ramping ahead of QLC: early QLC shipments begin late 2026 but QLC only becomes meaningful late 2027 into 2028, gated by the availability and affordability of 2-terabit QLC dies. CFO Jason Tsai was explicit that the delay is a NAND-industry availability issue, not a controller issue.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 Tier 1 customers in production, 5 more ramping in H2; MonTitan targeted at 5-10% of revenue exiting 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation 4-nanometer PCIe Gen 6 MonTitan controller completes tape-out in August 2026, developed in close collaboration with customers and aimed at hyperscalers and cloud service providers. Multiple design wins are already secured with both flash makers and cloud service providers, and more than a dozen Tier 1 customers are waiting for samples. The architecture targets AI inference - management specifically cited NVIDIA's CMX architecture - plus multi-host operation under new AI workloads. Management expects the Gen 6 ramp to be 'much stronger and faster, bigger than our PCIe Gen 5 ramps' and set an initial target market share of at least 15-20%, with the controller becoming a significant growth driver in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 4nm PCIe Gen 6 tape-out August 2026; >12 Tier 1 customers awaiting samples; initial share target 15-20%; growth driver in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Ferri for Automotive and Enterprise Boot Drive solutions MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially and now represent nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago. These are controller-plus-NAND solutions, so ASPs are much higher than controller-only (and higher than MonTitan). The DRAM-less boot drive is the crown jewel: conventional DRAM-based boot drives for server CPUs stay with the NAND makers, but DPUs, TPUs, NPUs and switches favour DRAM-less designs for cost, security and performance - and NAND makers have no DRAM-less PCIe SSD controllers and little incentive to build them for a market where densities are only 256GB-512GB. A server rack can carry more than 30 or 40 boot drives, and per-drive capacity should rise. Management sees little competition from either NAND makers or module makers, and said Ferri plus Boot Drive reaching roughly one third of revenue in 2027 is 'certainly a possibility' given current backlog and pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: Ferri + Boot Drive more than doubled QoQ to ~30% of revenue (from 4% a year ago); >30-40 boot drives per server rack

quarterly_data.signal: Edge SSD controllers grew 40-45% year over year in Q2 after a seasonally soft Q1, and SSD revenue is up about 50% versus the first half of last year on share gains despite declining PC units. The PCIe 4 to PCIe 5 transition is proceeding MORE SLOWLY than management expected six months ago: OEMs are pairing the latest, more cost-effective NAND with PCIe 4 SSDs in value and mainstream PCs to cut bill-of-materials cost. The 4-channel PCIe 5 controller introduced in Q4 of last year continues to ramp steadily in the mid- to high-end PC segment, and management still expects SSD average selling prices to rise through the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Edge SSD +40-45% YoY; SSD revenue ~+50% vs prior-year first half; PCIe 4-to-5 transition slower than expected

quarterly_data.signal: Embedded eMMC & UFS grew significantly ahead of the industry on share gains, as NAND makers increasingly outsource to third-party controllers while concentrating their own resources on DRAM and HBM. The majority of segment revenue is UFS (higher ASP, mostly smartphones) with eMMC going to IoT and connected devices - automotive, smart glasses, watches, drones, robots, next-generation set-top boxes and smart TVs. Silicon Motion already supports three of the NAND makers with its automotive controller and firmware after a decade of automotive certification work.

Physical-AI storage opportunity: management is engaged with multiple robotics companies and believes the robotics opportunity for Ferri 'may be larger than automotive,' spanning vision systems, LiDAR, compute storage and control systems, with more than one storage device per robot. Drones are expected to arrive earlier and in higher volume than humanoid robots; initial 2027 volumes remain small with much higher volumes expected by 2030.

Balance sheet: cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $181.8 million at the end of Q2, down from $210.9 million at the end of Q1, reflecting $16.9 million of dividend payments and an increase in inventories to support the growing business. Stock-based compensation excluded from non-GAAP results was $3.4 million; Q3 stock-based compensation and dispute-related expenses are guided to $14.9-15.9 million.

connects_to.relationship: DRAM-less enterprise Boot Drive storage for BlueField DPUs

contracts.signal: Asked whether BlueField-4 was contributing as NVIDIA ramps the Vera Rubin platform, CEO Wallace Kou said Silicon Motion has 'a pretty large share for BlueField supply for Boot Drives' and expects to benefit as BlueField ramps in the second half of 2026, declining to comment on generation timing beyond the customer's own announcements. Boot Drive wins extend beyond DPUs to TPUs, telco customers and leading server makers, and management said the business 'could grow even more strongly next year' with the leading GPU company.
